note: Scripts of takes Tom kept, for lines no chapter script file holds (merge-local.js). Loads last, so it wins.

lines.text: Up, up. Everybody up. Deedee will make it better.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent] Up, up. Everybody up. [warm Long Island accent] Deedee will make it better.

lines.text: Hello, Rose. Please keep your arms and legs inside the uncle at all times.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan] Hello, Rose. [official announcement] Please keep your arms and legs inside the uncle at all times.

lines.text: Oof, I'm finally here! At least the 6 hours went by fast on Delta One!
lines.script: [weary, relieved] Oof, I'm finally here! [smirking, bragging] At least the 6 hours went by fast on Delta One!

lines.text: Thanks for the JFK pickup, Sal.
lines.script: [casual, calm] Thanks for the JFK pickup, Sal.

lines.text: You got it, kid. Head outside, I think there's a couple of pipsqueaks looking for you.
lines.script: [thick long island accent, quick, friendly] You got it, kid. Head outside, I think there's a couple of pipsqueaks looking for you.

lines.text: Mom, wait. Bosses hit in a pattern. Watch what he does twice, then go.
lines.script: [interrupting] Mom, wait. [informing] Bosses hit in a pattern. [calm, instructing] Watch what he does twice, then go.

lines.text: I've been nine for SIX hours.
lines.script: [proud, smug] I've been nine for [emphasized]SIX hours.

lines.text: I asked a tree for directions.
lines.script: [fast, dreamy] I asked a tree for directions.

lines.text: Deedee keeps offering me apple muffins. I keep saying yes. That's called manners.
lines.script: [heavy Long Island accent, serene, smug] Deedee keeps offering me apple muffins. I keep saying yes. [heavy Long Island accent, arch, deadpan] ...That's called MANNERS.

lines.text: 3 wrappers, let's follow them!
lines.script: [bright, bossy, bright, energetic] 3 wrappers, let's follow them!

lines.text: One more ride, Tata! To the cab!
lines.script: [small, earnest, silly, bright, energetic] One more ride, Tah Tah! To the cab!

lines.text: Los Angeles? You got it.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] Los Angeles? You got it.

lines.text: Apple muffins in the oven, dinner on the stove, floors just mopped. Shoes off. Who wants a cookie?
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, brisk, fussing] Apple muffins in the oven, dinner on the stove, floors just mopped. [warm Long Island accent, bossy, sweet] Shoes off. [warm Long Island accent, bright, coaxing] Who wants a cookie?

lines.text: Alright, time for me to head back to LA. Let's head to Sal's!
lines.script: [dry, calm, bright, energetic] Alright, time for me to head back to LA. Let's head to Sal's!

lines.text: Apple muffins is cooling on the counter. Don't touch it. Okay, one corner.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, stern, warm] Apple muffins is cooling on the counter. Don't touch it. [warm Long Island accent, softening, playful] Okay, one corner.

lines.text: Oh, honey. Nobody has to turn off the lights. We'll come back. Every full moon. I'll bring apple muffins.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, tender, melting] Oh, honey. [warm Long Island accent, warm, reassuring] Nobody has to turn off the lights. We'll come back. Every full moon. [warm Long Island accent, brisk, gentle] I'll bring apple muffins.

lines.text: Tata. At the apple muffins.
lines.script: [sheepish, small] Tah Tah. At the apple muffins.

lines.text: Apple muffins! Deedee brings the teachers APPLE MUFFINS?
lines.script: [astonished, delighted] Apple muffins! [scandalized, shrill] Deedee brings the teachers APPLE MUFFINS?

lines.text: Dad’s in his recliner. Mom has the apple muffins. They’re fine. They’re probably fine.
lines.script: [quiet, steady] Dad’s in his recliner. Mom has the apple muffins. [thin, hopeful] They’re fine. [uncertain, low] They’re probably fine.

lines.text: Long Island is under glass now, you know. Mr. Vance put a dome over it. It’s very safe. Your mother is in her kitchen, making apple muffins.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Long Island is under glass now, you know. Mr. Vance put a dome over it. It's very safe. Your mother is in her kitchen, making apple muffins.

lines.text: Besides, you just got here. Go see your mother. She made apple muffins.
lines.script: [warm, friendly] Besides, you just got here. Go see your mother. [relishing, drawn out] She made APPLE MUFFINS.

lines.text: Tom! Sit. Eat. I made apple muffins. Yes, I know it's nine in the morning. Do not argue.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, warm, bustling] Tom! Sit. Eat. [warm Long Island accent, proud, firm] I made apple muffins. Yes, I know it's nine in the morning. [warm Long Island accent, sweet, warning] Do not argue.

lines.text: Deedee. I’m going to eat the apple muffins now. Okay? Okay.
lines.script: [gentle, resolved] Deedee. I’m going to eat the apple muffins now. [soft, brave] Okay? Okay.

lines.text: She’s looping. Look at the tray. Same apple muffins. Every time. They’re fresh, they’re perfect, and nobody ever eats them.
lines.script: [quiet, sad] She’s looping. Look at the tray. [careful, flat] Same apple muffins. Every time. [aching, soft] They’re fresh, they’re perfect, and nobody ever eats them.

lines.text: Nobody gets hurt. Nobody gets old. Nobody gets left. Your mother’s inside. She’s fine. She’s making apple muffins.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, flat, recited] Nobody gets hurt. Nobody gets old. Nobody gets left. [thick New York accent, gentle, proud] Your mother’s inside. She’s fine. [thick New York accent, flat, mechanical] She’s making apple muffins.

lines.text: A layover! Where? Never mind. Take a sweater. Actually, take two. And take the apple muffins.
lines.script: [warm Long Island accent, bright, thrilled] A layover! Where? Never mind. [warm Long Island accent, brisk, fussing] Take a sweater. Actually, take two. And take the apple muffins.

lines.text: Inside. She’s fine. She’s making apple muffins. Don’t look at the porch.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, evasive] Inside. She’s fine. She’s making apple muffins. [thick New York accent, hurried] Don’t look at the porch.

lines.text: And the apple muffins are excellent.
lines.script: [thick New York accent, dry] And the apple muffins are excellent.
